subject: Political Science
central_question: How do constitutional election rules translate popular choice into representation while protecting free, fair and inclusive democratic competition?
in_scope_units: The relationship between elections, direct democracy, indirect democracy and representative government.
Constitutional rules concerning voter eligibility, candidature, supervision, voting and counting.
First Past the Post electoral system and its effects on votes and seats.
Proportional Representation, party-list systems and the Single Transferable Vote used in indirect elections.
Reasons for India‘s adoption of FPTP for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.
Reservation of constituencies for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Universal adult franchise, right to contest and constitutional qualifications.
The independent Election Commission of India and its powers.
Problems in electoral competition and proposals for electoral reform.
banned_topics: A general philosophical account of equality unrelated to elections and representation.
Detailed parliamentary law-making or executive formation except where electoral rules affect representation.
Current election results or laws not contained in the supplied source.

known_pitfalls.correction: Non-democratic rulers may also hold elections; democratic elections require genuine choice, fairness and representation.

known_pitfalls.claim: The FPTP winner must receive more than half of all votes.
known_pitfalls.correction: The winner needs more votes than every rival and may win with less than a majority.

known_pitfalls.claim: In PR, voters always choose an individual constituency candidate.
known_pitfalls.correction: In the party-list forms discussed, voters choose a party and seats are distributed in proportion to vote share.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Election Commission supervises Panchayat elections.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Election Commission of India handles national and State legislative elections; local elections are under State Election Commissions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Reserved constituencies give some voters extra votes.
known_pitfalls.correction: All eligible voters vote once; reservation changes who may contest, not the number or value of votes.

known_pitfalls.claim: The right to vote is described as an unrestricted Fundamental Right.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter treats voting and contesting through constitutional and legal provisions, including qualifications.
